# inherit

Type-safe constructor implementation based on type level lambda calculus

*For proof of concept only, no further development plans are in place.*

***See https://github.com/2A5F/partial_this***

The complete form looks like:
```rust
pub struct Foo {
    pub foo: i32,
    pub bar: f32,
}

// generated by proc macro
impl CtorTypes for Foo {
    type Partial: PartialThis<FieldChain<FieldChain<CtorThis<Some>, field_foo>, field_bar>>,
    type Done: PartialThis<CtorThis<Some>>,
}
impl Foo {
    pub fn new_in_place(addr: NonNull<Self>) {
        let this: PartialThis<FieldChain<FieldChain<CtorThis<Foo>, field_foo>, field_bar>> =
            PartialThis::new(FieldChain::new(FieldChain::new(CtorThis::new(addr))));
        _ = <Self as Ctor>::ctor(this);
    }
    pub fn new() -> Box<Self> {
        let this = Box::new_uninit();
        Self::new_in_place(this.as_mut_ptr());
        this.assume_init()
    }
}

// impl by user
impl Ctor for Foo {
    fn ctor(this: Self::Partial) -> Self::Done {
        this.foo(1).bar(1.0)

        // or, any order
        this.bar(1.0).foo(1)

        // type safe, removed field_foo
        let a: PartialThis<FieldChain<CtorThis<Some>, field_bar>> = this.foo(1);
    } 
}
```

See the code for more details
